summary: AI observability gives teams visibility into how their LLM applications behave in production by tracing requests, evaluating output quality, tracking token usage, and monitoring latency and cost. As LLM API spend scales quickly and model outputs are non-deterministic, observability is essential for controlling costs, catching regressions, and debugging complex agent workflows.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end traces, prompt/response chains, token usage, latency, and evaluation metrics for LLM and agent applications (especially LangChain-based).
features: Deep tracing of chains and agent steps
Prompt playground and versioning
Automated and human-in-the-loop evaluations
Dataset creation and regression testing
Dashboards for cost and latency monitoring
Tight integration with the LangChain ecosystem
tools.pricing: Free Developer tier includes ~5,000 traces/month; paid Plus plan adds seat-based and usage pricing. Trace costs in trace-heavy workloads can run roughly 5–10% of underlying LLM API spend.
tools.best_for: Teams building on LangChain/LangGraph who want rich tracing, evaluation, and prompt iteration in one platform.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API request/response logs, token counts, per-request and aggregate cost, latency, cache hits, and rate limits via a proxy/gateway.
features: One-line gateway/proxy integration
Automatic cost computation per request and model
Request caching to cut costs
Rate limiting and custom properties for segmentation
User-level and session-level analytics
Prompt logging and metrics dashboards
tools.pricing: Free tier up to 10,000 requests/month; usage-based pricing of approximately $79 per 100,000 traces on paid plans.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting fast, low-effort cost tracking and gateway-level metering across any LLM provider.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: Model experiments, training metrics, LLM traces and evaluations (via W&B Weave), token usage, latency, and output quality.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Experiment tracking and model versioning
Prompt and output logging with comparison views
Evaluation pipelines and scorers
Rich dashboards and collaborative reports
Integrations across the ML/LLM stack
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; team and enterprise plans are seat- and usage-based (contact sales for enterprise). Weave usage is metered on ingested traces.
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams that need both traditional experiment tracking and LLM observability in a unified platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production model and LLM performance, embeddings drift, data quality, traces, evaluations, and quality/safety metrics.
features: LLM tracing and evaluation (Arize Phoenix open source)
Drift, data quality, and performance monitoring
Embedding and cluster analysis for root-cause debugging
Automated LLM-as-a-judge evaluations
Alerting and dashboards for production monitoring
OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source; Arize AX cloud offers a free tier with paid Pro and Enterprise plans priced by usage and seats.
tools.best_for: ML and LLMOps teams needing production-grade monitoring, drift detection, and troubleshooting at scale.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: Traces, nested spans, prompt versions, token usage, cost, latency, and evaluation scores for LLM and agent apps.
features: Open-source, self-hostable tracing backend
Detailed nested trace and span views
Prompt management and versioning
Cost and token tracking per model
Evaluation and scoring (manual, model-based, user feedback)
SDKs for Python/JS and OpenTelemetry support
tools.pricing: Open source and free to self-host; managed cloud has a free Hobby tier with paid Core, Pro, and Enterprise plans based on events/traces ingested.
tools.best_for: Developers wanting an open-source, framework-agnostic observability stack they can self-host for data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and cost via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation that exports to existing observability backends.
features: Open-source OpenTelemetry extension for LLMs
Auto-instrumentation of popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Vendor-neutral export to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.
Standardized semantic conventions for LLM spans
Non-intrusive integration into existing telemetry pipelines
Works with Traceloop's managed platform
tools.pricing: Free and open source (Apache-2.0); backend costs depend on your chosen observability vendor. Traceloop offers free and paid managed tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams that already use OpenTelemetry and want standardized, vendor-neutral LLM telemetry in their current stack.

cost_tips: Cache repeated or similar requests (and use prompt/response caching at the gateway) to avoid paying for identical completions multiple times.
Route tasks to the cheapest model that meets quality needs, reserving large frontier models only for complex queries and using smaller or distilled models for simpler ones.
Trim prompt and context size by removing redundant instructions, compressing retrieved context, and setting sensible max-token limits to reduce input and output token spend.
Instrument and monitor cost per request, user, and feature so you can set budgets and alerts, then optimize the highest-spend paths first.
